public_rationale: He reported planned terms from internal documents and warned they might change. GitHub's terms matched them. On April 27 GitHub said Business and Enterprise seat prices stay at $19 and $39, with promotional credits of $30 and $70 a month for June, July and August (e1, e2). An August summary of GitHub's docs says existing Business and Enterprise customers got 3,000 and 7,000 pooled credits per user per month from June 1, which is $30 and $70 at $0.01 per credit (e3). Billing went live June 1 (e4). His caveat would have protected him if the amounts had changed, but they did not.
limitations: The GitHub blog text could not be read, so the evidence is a news report and dated secondary summaries rather than GitHub's own page.
The promotion applied to existing customers only; his wording was broader.

our_interpretation: He is reporting planned terms from internal documents and flags that the amounts may change. The test is whether GitHub announced and ran the terms he described.

Because he warned the amounts might change, different launch amounts would not count against him. They would leave the claim not adjudicable rather than contradicted. The hedge only protects him if the terms differ.
'$30 of pooled AI credits' is read as the total monthly included allowance per Business seat (3,000 credits at $0.01 each), not $30 on top of the base $19. The same applies to $70 for Enterprise.
The promotion applying only to existing Business and Enterprise customers is treated as consistent with his wording.
criteria.support_condition: GitHub's announced and live terms for June through August 2026: Business stays at $19 per user per month with about $30 (3,000 credits) of pooled monthly credits, and Enterprise stays at $39 with about $70 (7,000 credits).
criteria.contradiction_condition: None, given his stated caveat. If GitHub had launched with different amounts, the caveat he gave means the claim would be not adjudicable rather than contradicted. Only a launch with no promotion and no pooled credits, i.e. a different structure entirely, would weigh against the core report.
